description: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 9,000 reported cases, with more than 4,380 deaths, according to government figures. description:
A former Ukrainian army officer has gone on trial in Germany, accused of coordinating the 2022 explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea. German prosecutors allege that Serhii K. led a six-person group that used a rented yacht to reach waters near Denmark's Bornholm island, where divers planted explosives on or near the pipelines. Prosecutors argue that the attack targeted civilian infrastructure supplying Russian gas to Western Europe and constitutes a war crime. Serhii K. denies the charges, while his defence lawyers question the strength of the evidence, saying investigators found no DNA or fingerprints linking him to the operation. Ukraine's government has consistently denied involvement in the explosions. The trial presents a diplomatic challenge for Germany as it seeks accountability for the attack while maintaining support for Ukraine in its war against Russia. Proceedings are expected to last several months.

The strikes, among the largest targeting the capital's energy infrastructure in recent months, have triggered unscheduled blackouts and severe disruptions to water supplies. The delayed warning has raised concerns that the United States may be withholding critical intelligence used by Ukraine's air force to detect incoming attacks, although this has not been independently confirmed. Al Jazeera's Audrey McAlpin reports from Kyiv.

description: The number of people developing dementia worldwide each year could more than double by 2050, according to a new study. Researchers project that annual cases will rise from nearly 11 million in 2023 to almost 25 million by 2050, largely driven by ageing populations. Alzheimer's disease accounts for up to 70 percent of dementia cases, while scientists estimate that a significant proportion could be prevented or delayed by addressing risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking and hearing loss. Women face a higher risk of developing dementia, and low- and middle-income countries are expected to experience particularly sharp increases. Dr Ivan Koychev, a neuroscientist and Clinical Associate Professor in Neuropsychiatry at Imperial College London, tells Al Jazeera that managing cardiovascular health, staying physically and socially active, and maintaining intellectual engagement can help reduce the risk.
